description: `e2e/resume-pdf-route.spec.ts` (the Preview-print fidelity tests) and `e2e/job-applications-i18n.spec.ts` (the quick-add validation and drag-and-drop announcement steps) pass on every run, locally and in CI. They keep checking the same product behaviour, and no assertion is weakened.

userStories.title: The resume PDF fidelity tests compare content, not pdf.js spacing
userStories.description: As the team, I want the route-versus-Preview-print comparison to ignore how pdf.js splits letter-spaced glyphs, so that it fails only when the two PDFs really differ.
acceptanceCriteria: The page-text comparison in `expectSamePdf` no longer depends on whitespace that pdf.js inserts between glyph items. It still fails when a character is added, removed, changed or reordered; It still fails when the text moves to another page.
A unit-level or fixture check proves it: two page texts that differ only by spaces inside letter-spaced words compare equal; texts that differ by one character, or by two swapped words, do not.
Page count, page size, the A4 check, the no-print-chrome check and the modern band check are unchanged.
`e2e/resume-pdf-route.spec.ts` passes 10 times in a row (`--repeat-each=10`), run alone.
Every other user of `readPdf` keeps its behaviour, or is checked to remain correct if the helper changes.
FR-1: No retries, no raised global timeouts, no skip or fixme. Per-assertion waits use Playwright's web-first assertions with their default timeout.
FR-2: No assertion is removed or loosened beyond what the story names. Specifically, US-001 ignores only pdf.js inter-item whitespace.
FR-3: A product change is made only for a diagnosed product defect. It is the smallest change, keeps every existing behaviour, and is covered by its own test.
Regression constraint: Every other e2e spec is unaffected, and so is every other user of `e2e/fixtures/pdf.ts`.
Regression constraint: `pnpm test:parity` and `pnpm test:visual` keep their baselines.
Regression constraint: The resume PDF route, the Preview print, the job-applications board and the quick-add form behave as before, unless FR-3 applies.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline.
Verification: Each changed spec passes `--repeat-each=10` alone.
Verification: Two consecutive full `pnpm test:e2e` runs on the final diff with neither of these two specs failing. Another spec failing is recorded, with its error.
Verification: CI's E2E job on the PR is green on its first attempt, or a failure in another spec is recorded.
Verification: `code-reviewer` on each story, confirming no assertion was weakened beyond FR-2.
Verification: `ui-expert` only if FR-3 changes product UI.
FAIL condition: Either spec fails in any `--repeat-each=10` run, or in a full-suite run on the final diff.
FAIL condition: The fidelity comparison would accept a changed or reordered character, or text on the wrong page.
FAIL condition: An assertion is removed, a locale dropped, a retry or skip added, or a global timeout raised.
BLOCKER condition: The quick-add failure turns out to be a product defect whose fix needs a product decision. Report it; the owner decides.
BLOCKER condition: The failures cannot be reproduced or understood locally, and no evidence ties a fix to them. Report it with what was tried.
Out of scope: The other one-off failures listed in Context.
Out of scope: Playwright retries, longer global timeouts, or `test.fixme`/`skip` as the fix.
Out of scope: Changing what the tests prove: page count, page size, text content and order; every localized message; every announcement.
Out of scope: CI configuration.
Out of scope: The cover-letter-swiss-format work.

userStories.title: The job-applications i18n spec waits for what it asserts
userStories.description: As the team, I want the quick-add and drag-and-drop steps to wait for the UI state they check, so that they never read too early.
acceptanceCriteria: Diagnosis. The cause of the quick-add failure is diagnosed and recorded: test timing, or the form showing its "too long" messages in sequence or late. If it is a product defect, the smallest product fix makes all three messages appear after one submit, and it is reported.
Quick-add assertions. The steps still assert: every "required" message; the three "too long" messages; the invalid-URL message; the no-English scan; in every locale the spec covers.

Drag-and-drop announcements. Each announcement assertion waits for the expected text (for example a web-first `toHaveText` on the live region), instead of reading the region once. Each still asserts the exact localized pick-up, over, drop and cancel wording.
